Position Summary:  



  

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as the senior operational leader of the Institute of National Security, reporting to the Founding Director and Executive Director. The COO is responsible for translating the Institute's strategic vision into coordinated execution across its four Pillars — Educate, Innovate, Convene, and Advise — and its five Centers of Excellence: currently the Asness Summit on Modern Conflict and Emerging Threats and the Wicked Problems Lab; along with the future AI Gaming Center of Excellence, the National Security Leadership Academy, and the Commodore National Defense Research Center.  



  

The COO synchronizes activity across the Institute's growing portfolio of programs and personnel, supports team members leading Pillar\- and Center\-level initiatives, builds and sustains the partnerships and resources that fund the Institute's educational and research mission, and positions the Institute to recognize and respond to opportunities and challenges as it scales. This is a senior leadership role requiring a seasoned executive with a demonstrated record of operational leadership, team development, and partnership\-building within complex, mission\-driven organizations.  



  

About the Work Unit  



  

The Institute of National Security is a rapidly growing Vanderbilt University institute dedicated to advancing national security scholarship, leadership development, and public engagement. Organized around four strategic Pillars and five Centers of Excellence, the Institute convenes students, faculty, military, government, and industry partners to address the nation's most pressing security challenges. As the Institute expands its structure including its staff, programming, and partnerships, the COO plays a central role in ensuring the organization scales both its stature and structure effectively by remaining aligned with its mission.

Lead a recurring In\-Progress Review (IPR) process across all Pillars and Centers of Excellence to align activity, identify opportunities and challenges, surface risks, and maintain a unified operating rhythm for the Institute.
  

  

Establish and maintain a master operating calendar and coordination framework that integrates programming, events, and initiatives across the Institute's full portfolio.
  

  

Oversee execution of high\-profile, cross\-cutting events, prioritizing tasks, delegating responsibility, and ensuring seamless integration across teams, Pillars, and Centers.
  

  

Continuously adapt operating structures and workflows to manage increased programming complexity as the Institute expands in depth and breadth.
  

  

Establish and manage transparent budget plans across the Institute's programs, tracking spending and revenue against strategic priorities.
  

  

Develop and track measurable outcomes for the Institute's projects and programs, ensuring initiatives stay on track and deliver against objectives.  

  



2\. Provide Support for Team Members Leading Activities Across Pillars and Centers of Excellence  



  

The COO provides guidance and feedback to team members who lead activities across the four Pillars and the Centers of Excellence, ensuring alignment with the Institute's mission and appropriate allocation of available resources.
  

  

Supervise and develop a growing team of project managers, program leads, and administrative staff, providing coaching, mentoring, and performance management.
  

  

Create workforce and staffing plans to ensure Pillar and Center leads have the resources needed to execute their programs; recommend hiring, promotion, and reward decisions in accordance with University guidelines.
  

  

Serve as the central point of support for Pillar and Center leads, resolving resource conflicts and providing guidance on operational matters.
  

  

Establish and continuously improve onboarding processes for new team members, visiting scholars, and other personnel joining the Institute.
  

  

Navigate and resolve conflicts across integrated teams, partners, and stakeholders, fostering a culture of trust as the Institute engages a growing and diverse set of collaborators.

To continue driving impact for its stakeholders, the Institute must grow its portfolio of partnerships and raise the financial resources needed to support both educational and research programming. The COO leads efforts to pursue and capture these resources.
  

  

Lead the development of new relationships and the strengthening of existing partnerships with external organizations, including government, military, donor, and academic stakeholders.
  

  

Partner with University leadership, Development and Alumni Relations, and the Executive Director to identify, pursue, and secure funding and in\-kind resources supporting the Institute's educational and research programming.
  

  

Pursue external funding and research opportunities that align with the Institute’s mission.
  

  

Negotiate partnership terms and agreements with external organizations on behalf of the Institute, in coordination with University offices as needed.


Represent the Institute in engagements with students, faculty, leadership, military, government, and national security partners, donors, board members, staff, alumni, and vendors, adapting communication style to the audience.
  

  

Collaborate with other University offices
